rulings.restated: helper "Anyone on the return made traditional IRA contributions for 2025" = true and helper "You were covered by a retirement plan (1 if Yes)" > 0 (a count)
rulings.model: The IRS line asks 'Were you covered by a retirement plan' without requiring traditional IRA contributions; the restatement adds that condition and does not reflect the MFS spouse-plan deemed-coverage rule.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained. Married filing separately is refused for the whole return before the worksheet is reached: scope.ready refuses on s3.mfs (Form 1040 filing status married filing separately; i1040gi p. 14, Married Filing Separately), so the worksheet's married-filing-separately rule (i1040gi p. 97, "If you weren't covered by a retirement plan but your spouse was, you are considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025") is never needed; on the statuses the tool completes, line 1a is the filer's own coverage, as the line asks.

rulings.restated: helper "Anyone on the return made traditional IRA contributions for 2025" = true and helper "Your spouse was covered by a retirement plan (1 if Yes)" > 0 (a count)
rulings.model: The IRS line is 'If married filing jointly, was your spouse covered by a retirement plan?'; the restatement adds a contribution condition and does not condition the line on married filing jointly.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation — i1040gi p. 97, line 1b: "If married filing jointly, was your spouse covered by a retirement plan?" The added contribution condition does not matter because the worksheet applies only when traditional IRA contributions were made, and a spouse entry exists only on a joint return; the line is the spouse's own coverage, as the source asks.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Lines 2 through 6 are completed (traditional IRA contributions, and someone is covered by a retirement plan)" = true → helper "Line 2, your column"] [helper "Lines 2 through 6 are completed (traditional IRA contributions, and someone is covered by a retirement plan)" = false → helper "Zero"]
rulings.model: For married filing separately and living apart from the spouse all year, the IRS says 'enter $89,000'; the program uses $10,000 for all married-filing-separately cases.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained. Married filing separately is refused for the whole return before the worksheet is reached: scope.ready refuses on s3.mfs (Form 1040 filing status married filing separately; i1040gi p. 14, Married Filing Separately), so the $89,000 amount for a married filer who lived apart all year and the $10,000 amount (i1040gi p. 97, line 2) are never read; the single, head of household, qualifying surviving spouse and joint amounts agree, as the model says.

rulings.restated: Add s1 line 11, s1 line 13, s1 line 15, s1 line 16, s1 line 17, s1 line 18, s1 line 19a, and s1 line 25.
rulings.model: The IRS says to add Schedule 1 'lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25'; the restatement omits Schedule 1 line 12, line 14, and line 23.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained (as ruled before). Schedule 1 lines 12, 14 and 23 are outside this tool: scope.schedule1 asks about "an adjustment on Schedule 1 line 12, 14 or 23" and refuses Form 1040 lines 8 and 10, so worksheet line 3 (Form 1040 line 9) refuses whenever one applies and within scope they are zero, as the line's citation says. The lines in scope (11, 13, 15 to 19a and 25) are all added. i1040gi p. 97, line 4, "Enter the total of the amounts from Schedule 1, lines 11 through 19a, plus 23 and 25".

rulings.restated: Add helper "Wages, salaries, tips, etc. (box 1 of the Forms W-2 of you and your spouse)" and s1 line 2a.
rulings.model: The IRS line includes 'Nontaxable combat pay' in the total; the restatement adds only W-2 box 1 wages and Schedule 1 line 2a.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: refusal located elsewhere; project retained. Nontaxable combat pay is refused: ira.combat_gate (traditional IRA contributions and s8812.combat_pay, "Did you receive any nontaxable combat pay in 2025 (it is generally shown in Form W-2, box 12, code Q)?") refuses person.ira_line11, so line 12 and Schedule 1 line 20, on every return that has it; within scope line 8 is wages and line 2a, as the line's citation says. i1040gi p. 98, line 8, "Nontaxable combat pay. This amount should be reported in box 12 of Form W-2 with code Q".

rulings.restated: Add person.ira_se over every confirmed person entry, within the current person when parent-bound. An unanswered roster is unknown.
rulings.model: The IRS line includes earned income 'as a self-employed individual or a partner'; the restatement uses only Schedule C amounts and zeros anyone without a Schedule C.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner ruling (register entry amb.2025.ira_se_floor); project retained. person.ira_se, now shown in the glossary, is each person's Schedule C profit or loss less that person's Schedule 1 lines 15 and 16 deductions, floored at zero per person (i1040gi p. 98, line 9, "Enter the earned income you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received as a self-employed individual or a partner, minus any deductions on Schedule 1, lines 15 and 16. If zero or less, enter -0-"); whether one spouse's loss nets against the other's earnings is the ambiguity the owner settled. Partnership earned income is refused before this line by the Schedule SE screen (person.se_screened, 'partnership and other self-employment income'), so only Schedule C earnings reach it.
